# ADR-000 — <decision, stated as a decision>

<!-- ADRs are for BIG, costly-to-reverse decisions — the ones where changing your mind
     means rewriting a subsystem. Small calls go in engineering/decision-log.md as a
     one-liner. When in doubt, use the decision log; a one-liner costs nothing. -->

**Status:** draft | active | superseded by ADR-###

## Context
<!-- What forces were in play? Constraints, not preferences. What was true at the time
     that made this a real choice rather than an obvious one? -->

## Decision
<!-- One sentence, active voice. Then the specifics as a numbered list. -->

## Consequences

### What this buys
<!-- Be concrete. "Simpler" is not a consequence; "no server to patch" is. -->

### What this costs
<!-- Every real decision has a cost. If you can't name one, you haven't found it yet. -->

### Invariants — do not break these
<!-- The load-bearing details that a future refactor would destroy without noticing.
     This is the highest-value section of most ADRs. -->

| # | Invariant | Why it exists |
|---|---|---|
| I1 |  |  |

### Known gaps — stated honestly
<!-- Security, correctness, or operational weaknesses this decision accepts.
     Writing them down is what makes them accepted rather than hidden. -->

## Alternatives considered

| Option | Why not |
|---|---|
|  |  |

## Revisit if
<!-- The concrete trigger that should reopen this. An ADR with no revisit condition
     is a decision nobody will ever revisit — including when they should. -->
